scope: Conceptual/formal audit of an act-theorem proposal. It does not deny phenomenological temporal self-presentation; it distinguishes its conditional support from a derivation of a specified flow grammar.

metaphysical_actuality_act.reason: actuality/act need not be process or succession

phenomenological_temporal_act.reason: temporal field/coherence underdetermines grammar and continuation law

success_conditions_for_a_genuine_act_the: independent finite temporalization bridge: finite self-presentation entails temporally differentiated act
noncircular representation theorem from act structure to successor/integration/boundary relations
anti-confirmation test: constraints remain defensible if they exclude IAR
restricted_conclusion: Self-presentation-as-act is a legitimate new route and can support conditional retentional/coherence constraints. But act is ambiguous: atemporal actuality gives no flow, while a temporally articulated act does not select AP3P1 flow or settle adequacy/boundaries. The required finite temporalization and act-to-grammar bridges are not currently derived; without them the proposal either presupposes flow or falls short of it.
